leo (customer): Hey support — our function calls started failing after last night's migration. Client gets a 404: {"error":"tool_not_found"}. We call tool 'Invoice.Generate' and it worked yesterday. Example request:
```
POST /v1/call
{
  "tool_name": "Invoice.Generate",
  "args": { "order_id": "abc123" }
}
```
Request id: req_0a9f2b. Can you check?

marie (support): Thanks — can you paste the full request id and workspace name? Are you calling by alias or UUID? Also which SDK version?

leo (customer): Workspace: acme-corp. SDK: js@2.4.1. We pass tool_name as shown (string alias). Full request id: req_0a9f2b-2026-03-15T23:12Z. No UUID used.

jake (eng-runtime): tagging eng-runtime. Quick thought: this smells like an alias/registry propagation problem (casing or duplicate alias). Can you paste the raw request headers and the exact JSON payload? Also if you can try with the tool UUID as a workaround that would be helpful.

leo (customer): headers: "authorization: Bearer sk-acme-...". Payload same as above. I don't have the UUID handy.

vince (registry): I pulled the registry logs for acme-corp around that window. We ran the alias consolidation migration at 23:00 UTC that merged 'invoice.generate' and 'Invoice.Generate' but the republish to edge caches failed in two regions — some nodes still point at the old uuid (tf_old_7f) while others point to the new uuid (tf_new_a2). That can produce a tool lookup mismatch.

marie (support): Vince, could the mismatch cause 404s or schema mismatches?

vince (registry): Yes. If a serving node routes to tf_old_7f which was retired and removed from the model pool, the serving layer returns tool_not_found. There was also a case where the old uuid pointed to a different tool that had an incompatible schema — that would cause schema validation failures (400). Workaround: call by UUID (tf_new_a2) or force the registry edge refresh:
```
curl -X POST "https://registry.internal/refresh?workspace=acme-corp" 
```
Clears alias cache for acme-corp.

marie (support): Leo, can you try the UUID fallback or the lower-case alias 'invoice.generate'?

leo (customer): Tried UUID approach after vinces note — used tf_new_a2 and call succeeded. Using lower-case alias also worked. So workaround is confirmed.

jake (eng-runtime): Root cause writeup: registry migration left stale alias mappings on some edge nodes. Serving lookup is case-sensitive and uses an edge cache. When a node looked up 'Invoice.Generate' it hit a stale mapping -> routed to a retired/incorrect uuid -> either 404 or schema mismatch depending on what that uuid used to point at.

jake (eng-runtime): Patch plan: 1) hotfix edge lookup to accept case-insensitive alias matches for 24h while we refresh caches, 2) trigger full alias republish + cache invalidation, 3) add a forced alias-version header so clients can opt into the canonical mapping. Rolling hotfix now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: registry-service v1.14.3-registry-fix -> canary (asia)

nina (sre): Monitoring shows spike of 404s for acme-corp at 23:05-23:40 UTC, then drop after canary.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: registry-service v1.14.3-registry-fix -> global

vince (registry): Alias cache cleared across regions for acme-corp and duplicate alias entry removed. We're seeing successful calls (by original casing) for the last 20m. No more 404s for the sample req ids.

leo (customer): Confirmed from our side — calls with 'Invoice.Generate' are working again. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

marie (support): Glad that's resolved. We'll keep monitoring and follow up with a postmortem section on preventing alias drift. Closing ticket unless anyone objects. :thumbsup:
